market.holdingsNote: Holds thousands of U.S. investment-grade bonds (Treasuries, corporates, mortgage-backed), with no stock exposure.

market.name: Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF
market.blurb: Only holds companies with a decade-plus streak of raising dividends, a quality screen that tends to select steadier, more established businesses, so the fund moves less than the market even though it's still 100% stocks. Holds large U.S. companies with at least 10 consecutive years of dividend increases, filtered for financial health.
market.holdingsNote: Holds large U.S. companies with at least 10 consecutive years of dividend increases, filtered for financial health.

market.name: Vanguard Wellesley Income Fund
market.blurb: Keeps roughly 60-65% of assets in investment-grade bonds and only 35-40% in dividend-paying stocks, so its price barely budges compared to a pure stock fund or an individual company's share price. A balanced fund holding about 60-65% investment-grade bonds and 35-40% dividend-paying stocks.
market.holdingsNote: A balanced fund holding about 60-65% investment-grade bonds and 35-40% dividend-paying stocks.

market.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
market.blurb: Owns a slice of all 500+ S&P 500 companies at once, so a bad day for one company barely dents the fund, unlike an individual stock where one earnings miss can swing the price double digits. Tracks all 500+ companies in the S&P 500, weighted by market cap, across every major U.S. sector.
market.holdingsNote: Tracks all 500+ companies in the S&P 500, weighted by market cap, across every major U.S. sector.

market.name: Vanguard 500 Index Fund Admiral Shares
market.blurb: The mutual fund twin of an S&P 500 ETF: it owns the same 500-plus companies, so it moves almost exactly in line with the broad market and avoids the single-company risk that comes with owning one stock. Tracks the S&P 500 directly, holding roughly 500 large U.S. companies in the same proportions as the index.
market.holdingsNote: Tracks the S&P 500 directly, holding roughly 500 large U.S. companies in the same proportions as the index.

market.name: Fidelity Contrafund
market.blurb: A manager actively picks roughly a few hundred large-cap growth stocks rather than tracking an index, so it's more diversified than any single stock but can still drift from the market depending on the manager's bets. Actively managed; the portfolio manager selects several hundred large-cap growth-oriented stocks, with heavy exposure to a few mega-cap tech names.
market.holdingsNote: Actively managed; the portfolio manager selects several hundred large-cap growth-oriented stocks, with heavy exposure to a few mega-cap tech names.

market.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
market.blurb: Spreads money across the 100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies, but its heavy tilt toward a handful of mega-cap tech names means it still swings noticeably harder than the broad market. Tracks the Nasdaq-100: the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq, dominated by big tech.
market.holdingsNote: Tracks the Nasdaq-100: the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq, dominated by big tech.

market.name: iShares Russell 2000 ETF
market.blurb: Diversifies across roughly 2,000 small companies rather than one, but small-caps as a group are more sensitive to economic swings and have less cash cushion than large-caps, so volatility stays elevated even with diversification. Holds about 2,000 small-cap U.S. companies that make up the Russell 2000 Index.
market.holdingsNote: Holds about 2,000 small-cap U.S. companies that make up the Russell 2000 Index.

market.name: Cal-Maine Foods
market.blurb: Q1 FY27 net sales (reported Sept 30) plunged 41.5% to $539.6M as an industry egg glut drove conventional egg prices down ~59%, flipping CALM to a $58.6M net loss; the stock sits near $67.48 awaiting Q2 FY27 results due January 2027.

market.name: Chemed Corp
market.blurb: Q2 2026 revenue rose 8.8% YoY to $673.3M as VITAS hospice revenue grew 11.9% on higher patient census and a lower Medicare Cap hit, prompting Chemed to raise full-year guidance; shares now trade near $539.82.

market.name: Saia Inc
market.blurb: Q2 2026 revenue grew 17.1% YoY to a record $956.5M as Saia's LTL terminal network expansion kept driving tonnage and share gains, though shares have pulled back to $344.38 from their 52-week high amid cost pressures.

market.name: Wingstop
market.blurb: Domestic same-store sales fell 7.5% in Q2 2026 as low-income-consumer pullback persisted, prompting Wingstop to cut full-year same-store sales guidance to -4% to -6%; shares now trade near $104.36, well below their 52-week high of $388.14.

market.name: Hanmi Financial
market.blurb: Shares sit near $31.60 after Q2 net income climbed to $23.5M ($0.79 EPS) on net interest income of $63.9M, up 1.0% sequentially on an improved funding mix; a ~$930M market cap still leaves it far more news-sensitive than a diversified bank ETF.

market.name: UMH Properties
market.blurb: Manufactured-housing REIT with a $1.32B market cap; small enough that a single piece of unexpected news can move the stock far more than a diversified REIT fund would.

market.name: CEVA Inc
market.blurb: Shares near $34.46, up roughly 19% from the prior update; this semiconductor-IP licensor's small size (~$960M market cap) means a single contract win or chip-industry headline can still swing the stock sharply in a session.

market.name: Ring Energy
market.blurb: Permian Basin oil producer still trading near $1.18 with a $320M market cap; a sub-$2 share price keeps it one of the most volatile names on this entire watchlist.

market.name: Live Nation Entertainment
market.blurb: Replaces Warner Bros. Discovery, which was delisted Oct 6, 2026 after its $110B all-cash acquisition by Paramount Skydance closed. Live Nation carries a real short thesis: the DOJ's ongoing monopoly lawsuit over its Ticketmaster dominance, paired with a rich ~$43B valuation, keeps bears circling even as live-event demand stays strong.

market.name: Skydance Corporation
market.blurb: Formerly Paramount Skydance (PSKY) -- the $110B Paramount Skydance/Warner Bros. Discovery merger closed Oct 6, 2026, and the combined media giant relisted as Skydance Corporation (SKYD) on the NYSE the same day. Trading data specific to the new combined entity was not yet reliably available at refresh time, so price/short-interest figures are carried over from the pre-close PSKY baseline.
